stem: Container A holds 2 liters more than twice the amount of water in container B. If 3 liters of water were poured from container A into container B, container A would then hold \(\frac{4}{3}\) of the amount in container B. How many liters of water does container B hold?
solution: Let \(v\) be the liters in container B; container A holds \(2v + 2\).
After pouring: A has \(2v - 1\) and B has \(v + 3\). Then \(2v - 1 = \frac{4}{3}(v + 3)\).
Multiply by 3: \(6v - 3 = 4v + 12\), so \(2v = 15\) and \(v = 7.5\). Check: A holds 17; after pouring, 14 and 10.5, and \(14 = \frac{4}{3}(10.5)\).
verify:
v = symbols('v')
sol = solve(Eq((2*v + 2) - 3, Rational(4, 3)*(v + 3)), v)
assert sol == [Rational(15, 2)]
assert all(Rational(a) == Rational(15, 2) for a in spr_answers)
